esig_regulation.term: eIDAS · Code de droit économique, livre XII, titre 2
esig_regulation.basis: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183. CDE art. XII.24 § 1 (loi du 21 juillet 2016): title 2 of book XII implements Regulation 910/2014 and adds rules for signature, seal, archiving, registered-delivery and time-stamping services. Code civil art. 8.1, 3°: an electronic signature is one within eIDAS art. 3(10)-(12).

data_access_basis.basis: A private party needs a lawful basis under GDPR Art. 6(1), for example legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)); data on criminal offences needs official authority or a legal authorisation (Art. 10). A person can request their own data (Art. 15) within the Art. 12(3) period. Processing by competent criminal-justice authorities falls under title 2 of the loi du 30 juillet 2018, which transposes Directive (EU) 2016/680 (art. 25).

timestamp_recognition.basis: Art. 41(1): a time stamp is not denied legal effect or admissibility solely because it is electronic or not qualified. Art. 41(2): a qualified time stamp is presumed accurate as to date and time and integrity of the bound data. Art. 42(1) sets the qualified requirements; Art. 24a(6) recognises qualified time stamps across Member States. CDE book XII, title 2 adds rules for time-stamping services of providers established in Belgium (art. XII.24 § 2).

evidence_rules.basis: Unless the law provides otherwise, proof may be given by any means (preuve libre).
A writing (écrit) may be on any medium if it stays accessible and its integrity is preserved. A legal act of EUR 3,500 or more must be proved by a signed writing.

evidence_rules.term: Titre préliminaire du Code de procédure pénale, art. 32
evidence_rules.basis: Irregularly obtained evidence is declared null only if a formal condition is prescribed on pain of nullity, the irregularity affected its reliability, or its use is contrary to a fair trial.
